caption: Wealth Management
vo: Managing someone's money means proving, at every step, that it suits them. Let's take a discretionary mandate from first meeting to an active, reviewed portfolio.

caption: Nathalie Ramdin, an existing client, wants Genesis to manage her portfolio
vo: Nathalie Ramdin is already a client, and now she wants Genesis to manage her portfolio. Her relationship manager, Natasha, opens the mandate.

caption: Sign in as Natasha Appadoo — Senior Relationship Manager
vo: So we sign in as Natasha Appadoo, who owns the client, and the mandate.

caption: Wealth Management ▸ Wealth Mandates: one card per mandate
vo: Every mandate is a card on this board, moving from Prospect all the way through to Active, and eventually Closed.

caption: The “Wealth mandate” button opens a two-step onboarding wizard
vo: One button starts a short wizard. First the client and profile, then the terms.

caption: No risk profile yet — she has not done the questionnaire
vo: She hasn't done the questionnaire yet, so we leave the risk profile empty.

caption: The terms: base currency, benchmark, custodian and the portfolio manager
vo: Now the terms. US dollars as the base currency, a sixty forty global benchmark, Genesis Capital Custody, and her portfolio manager. Reviews every quarter. Then the fees: one percent management, ten percent performance, and a minimum fee. She also asks for no tobacco or controversial weapons.

caption: Mandate created at Prospect
vo: The mandate starts at Prospect. The agreement and the IPS come later, from its Docs tab.

caption: The discovery meeting is held — move the card on
vo: Natasha holds the discovery meeting with Nathalie, then just drags the card on to the next stage.

caption: Next: profile her risk
vo: Next comes the big question. How much risk can she take?

caption: Wealth Management ▸ Risk Profiles: every client's profile
vo: Risk Profiles lists every client, with their score and model portfolio.

caption: “Investor Questionnaire” opens a three-step wizard
vo: The investor questionnaire is a three-step wizard, and Natasha fills it in together with Nathalie, never alone.

caption: Horizon and objectives
vo: When will she need the money, and what for?

caption: Attitude to risk and experience
vo: Then her attitude to risk, and her experience. The key question: if her portfolio fell twenty percent in a year, what would she do? She'd hold.

caption: Scored 55: model portfolio C — Balanced
vo: She scores fifty-five, which puts her in model portfolio C, Balanced. Her ceiling is risk three on a scale of one to five, and the profile is valid for two years.

caption: Prospects can take the same questionnaire on the website
vo: By the way, prospects can take this same questionnaire on the website. They see their profile instantly, and an adviser gets a Wealth enquiry.

caption: Every recommendation is recorded with its rationale and the risks disclosed
vo: Now, suitability. Every recommendation Natasha makes is recorded, with the reason for it and the risks disclosed. Here's the first one: discretionary management, because a balanced portfolio fits her horizon and objective.

caption: Discretionary management is rated risk 3 — within her ceiling of 3
vo: It's rated risk three, within her ceiling. It saves straight away.

caption: She also asks about the Emerging Markets Equity Fund
vo: But Nathalie also wants a small slice of emerging-market equities. So Natasha records a second recommendation, for the Emerging Markets Equity Fund. The catch? It's rated risk five, above her ceiling.

caption: Refused: the product is riskier than her profile allows
vo: And the CRM refuses it. Above the ceiling, you need an override reason and the client's signed acknowledgement.

caption: Override reason recorded and the client's acknowledgement ticked
vo: With both recorded, it saves, but it's flagged as a mismatch for everyone to see.

caption: Back to the mandate: prepare the proposal (IPS)
vo: Back to the mandate. Time to prepare the proposal, the IPS, so Natasha moves the card to Proposal.

caption: Blocked: a proposal needs the client's risk profile on the mandate
vo: Blocked. You can't propose a portfolio without the client's risk profile on the mandate. So Natasha opens the record.

caption: Link the risk profile she just completed
vo: Natasha links the profile Nathalie just completed, and the mandate picks up its model portfolio from it. C, Balanced. Nobody retypes it.

caption: The IPS is agreed and the mandate signed
vo: Nathalie agrees the IPS and signs, electronically, from the Docs tab.

caption: The client transfers her assets — Account funded
vo: Then she transfers her assets. But funding is only allowed once KYC is approved.

caption: Nathalie Ramdin's KYC is approved, so the move goes through
vo: Nathalie's KYC is approved, so this goes through. For a client whose KYC is still in progress, the board would simply refuse.

caption: Laurent, the portfolio manager, takes over
vo: From here, Laurent, the portfolio manager, takes over.

caption: Sign in as Laurent Koenig — Portfolio Manager
vo: So we sign in as Laurent Koenig. He manages the mandate and its reviews.

caption: Investments are in place: the mandate becomes Active
vo: The investments are in place. The mandate is Active.

caption: Each month-end the portfolio system sends an AUM snapshot
vo: Every month-end, the portfolio system sends an AUM snapshot. Market value by asset class, performance, and net flows. Here's Nathalie's first one: two point five million US dollars.

caption: Amounts are in the mandate's base currency — US dollars here
vo: It's all in the mandate's base currency. These snapshots drive performance and the net flows on the Wealth dashboard.

caption: The mandate's AUM is updated from the same feed
vo: The same feed updates the mandate's AUM, and that rolls up to Nathalie's Client 360.

caption: Mandate WM-2026-000021: model portfolio, AUM in USD and MUR, YTD performance, next review
vo: Here's the mandate at a glance. Model portfolio, AUM in dollars and rupees, year-to-date performance, and the next review. And every day, the system watches for attrition risk: falling AUM, missed reviews, or a complaint.

caption: Reviews follow the mandate's cycle — here quarterly
vo: Reviews follow the mandate's cycle, quarterly here. Normally the system opens one at Scheduled fourteen days before it's due. Laurent opens one now.

caption: Scheduled ▸ Pack prepared ▸ Meeting held ▸ Completed
vo: The pack is ready, so Nathalie is invited to the meeting.

caption: The meeting took place — move to Meeting held
vo: The meeting's done. Move it on.

caption: Blocked: Meeting held needs the date it was held
vo: Not so fast. Meeting held needs the date the meeting actually took place. It sounds small, but if a regulator asks when you last met this client, that's the answer. So Laurent opens the record and enters the date.

caption: Record the outcome and the minutes
vo: Then the outcome and the minutes. No change: allocation in line with model portfolio C, objectives and horizon unchanged. To complete a review you need both, plus the client's suitability re-confirmed.

caption: Blocked: re-confirm the client's profile and suitability before closing the review
vo: And there's the rule on Completed. No review closes without re-confirming suitability.

caption: Profile and suitability re-confirmed with the client
vo: So Laurent re-confirms Nathalie's profile and suitability with her, and ticks it. That's compliance built into the workflow, not left to a checklist.

caption: Review completed — the next one is due in three months
vo: Review completed. The next one's due in three months, and overdue reviews show on the dashboard and the RM workbench.

caption: The Strategic Asset Allocation Committee changes the house view
vo: Now, a bigger change. The Strategic Asset Allocation Committee shortens bond duration in the model portfolios, because rate cuts are largely priced in. Laurent records the decision.

caption: Saved — every portfolio manager is notified to brief the clients in the affected models
vo: As soon as it's saved, every portfolio manager is told to brief the clients in the affected models.

caption: The Wealth dashboard
vo: And here's the Wealth dashboard. Active mandates, AUM, overdue reviews, and attrition risk, right at the top.

caption: AUM by model portfolio, the mandate pipeline and net flows by month
vo: AUM by model, the mandate pipeline, and monthly net flows. Each widget opens the records behind it.

caption: Reviews by status, suitability mismatches that were overridden, profiles by model
vo: And yes, every overridden suitability mismatch is right there too.

caption: Wealth Management
vo: So, one mandate, from first meeting to its first review. Risk profiled, every recommendation justified, every gate enforced. Suitability is built into every step.
